state.title: morluto/rea — REA: Reverse Engineer Anything, one MCP for agent-driven reverse engineering
state.author: morluto
state.text_head:
See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.

REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.

Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.

> **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.

## Quick start

### Set up your agent

With Node.js and npm installed, run:

```bash
npx rea-agents setup
```

Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds
REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing
configuration. Restart your agent afterward.

Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and
[other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See
[installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and
manual MCP registration.

### Ask your agent

```text
Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a
similar feature for my project.
```

Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.

### Use the terminal

Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json
```

The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.
Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows.

To install the `rea` command for regular use:

```bash
npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help
```

For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the
[CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection,
snapshots and scripting.

### Update REA

REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your
installation up to date.

For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`:

```bash
rea update
```

Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release,
upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`.

To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed
by the update.

If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with:

```bash
npx rea-agents@latest setup
```

Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands,
use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use
`bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`.

state.text_head:
## 交流频道

QQ 频道：pd90484671（ai技术交流学习）
扫码加入频道，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 75 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本

Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Comment "HARNESS" and I'll send you the GitHub link!

Google just open sourced Harness², a harness that lets your AI agents upgrade themselves without any retraining 🤯

It proposes edits to your agent's prompts, tools, memory and skills, tests them on the same task, and keeps what worked. Then it saves the lessons from every task, so each round of improvement starts smarter than the last.

It's basically recursive self-improvement for your agent's setup, not the model itself, and one round boosted benchmark scores by up to 11.5 points with the exact same model.

post.text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://github.com/

post.text:
看到这个帖子这么火，我不得不给大家推荐一下Orca这开源个项目了

原帖里让一个 AI 指挥一群 AI 干活的玩法过于原始了，Orca已经提供了十分棒相应的多 Agent 编排基建。

大家可以把它理解成一个 AI 编程工作台：Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 等工具放在同一个地方运行，你能统一看任务、看进度、看代码改动。

原帖提到的几个关键环节，在 Orca 里有什么更好的实现方式呢？

1. 让一个 AI 当负责人，其他 AI 分头干活

通过它的编排功能，可以让负责统筹的 Agent 拆分任务、启动其他 Agent、收集结果，再安排后续工作。

比如做一个网站，可以让 Claude 负责拆需求，Codex 写接口，另一个 Agent 检查代码。具体谁做什么，由你和负责统筹的 Agent 来定。

2. 多个任务同时跑

每个任务可以有自己的独立代码目录和分支，也就是 git worktree。一个改登录页，一个修支付接口，分别干活，最后再审查、合并结果。

还可以把同一道题交给几个 Agent 同时做，对比方案后再选。

3. 干完回报，卡住提问

它有任务状态、Agent 之间的消息和完成回报机制。执行者做完会把结果交回负责人，遇到阻塞也能提问，省掉你在几个窗口之间来回复制消息。

任务在后台推进时，你也可以继续讨论需求、补充要求，再把调整传给对应的 Agent。

4. 搭配不同模型和工具

Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 都能接，支持列表里也有 DeepSeek Harness。想用本地模型，可以先在 OpenCode 等支持本地模型的工具里配好，再放进 Orca 使用。

模型和运行工具可以按任务搭配，不必所有活都消耗同一种模型的额度。

此外，它把查看代码差异、逐行批注、浏览器预览也放进了工作台。你可以直接指出哪一处需要改，让 Agent 接着处理。

而且手机端也很还有，远程VibeCoding爽歪歪🤩

免费开源，支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux。

https://www.onorca.dev

this is f*cking insane, every app u pay for monthly is already sitting on ur disk as code, and one free repo now lets Claude Code read all of it down to the binary in 5 minutes of setup

REA is an open-source MCP server that plugs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. it runs locally, uploads nothing and backs every answer with the function, file and call behind it

setup:

→ check Node: u need 22.19+, 24.11+ or 26+, versions 23 and 25 don't work
→ run npx rea-agents@latest setup and pick Claude Code
→ REA shows every change before making it and backs up ur config
→ restart the agent fully, closing the window isn't enough
→ run the doctor check, it only reads and tells u what to fix

engines by target:

> Electron apps like Notion, Slack, Discord: nothing extra
> .NET apps and many Unity games: nothing extra
> .exe programs and old games: Ghidra 12.1 with JDK 21
> Android APKs: JDK 17+ and JADX
> websites: any Chrome-family browser
> contract bytecode: Linux x64

limits:

> it can't touch server code, only what's on ur machine
> decompiled code is a reconstruction, so always verify
> stripped C++ binaries are much harder than Unity games

first test, send Claude Code this:

use REA to investigate how [feature] works in [app]. show the function, file and call behind every step, mark what is still unknown, write a spec with no copied code, then build my version and test it against the original

post.text:
Someone built Git for AI agent memory.

ModernRelay has open-sourced OmniGraph, a graph database that gives AI agents something most shared-memory systems lack: branches, commits, diffs, and three-way merges.

The idea is simple. If multiple agents are working on the same knowledge base, they should be able to make changes independently without corrupting or overwriting each others work.

Imagine three agents researching the same subject. One extracts information from documents, another resolves duplicate entities, and a third connects claims to supporting evidence.

With OmniGraph, each agent works on its own branch of the knowledge graph. Changes to entities, relationships, and evidence remain isolated until they're reviewed and merged.

And this is where the engineering gets interesting.

The merge engine compares changes against a common ancestor, much like Git. It can detect conflicting entity updates, delete-versus-modify conflicts, orphaned relationships, and schema violations.

Conflicting changes are reported explicitly. Successful merges are committed atomically, and previous graph states remain available through version history.

OmniGraph also combines several retrieval methods in one engine:
→ Graph traversal for following relationships
→ Vector search for semantic similarity
→ BM25 for keyword-based retrieval
→ Reciprocal Rank Fusion for combining results

Under the hood, its written in Rust and uses versioned Lance files for storage, with support for local and

post.text:
🚨 CHROME MIGHT BE OVERKILL FOR YOUR AI AGENT.

Meet Moli.

A Rust-built headless browser designed specifically for AI agents.

The clever part?

Moli doesn't constantly render the entire visual world.

It starts with the browser structure:

→ DOM
→ JavaScript
→ CSS
→ Network
→ Storage

Need geometry? Build layout.

Need a screenshot? Render it.

Need neither? Skip the expensive visual work.

That makes browser automation much more resource-efficient.

Moli supports:
→ CDP
→ WebDriver
→ WebDriver BiDi
→ Playwright
→ Linux, macOS, Windows

And the benchmark is interesting:

Moli: 81.88% task success
Chrome: 99.85%

But Moli used roughly 15% of Chrome's CPU time and 13% of its peak memory in the project's resource comparison.

That's the tradeoff:

Less browser overhead.
Still enough web runtime for serious AI-agent workloads.

#AI #Coding #AIAgents #Rust

In response to the ZCode product security issues reported by the community, we have completed the necessary remediation and sincerely apologize to all our users.

We have open-sourced ZCode at https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode, placing the code under community scrutiny and making ZCode more open and transparent.

We sincerely thank the community developers who previously identified issues in ZCode. Going forward, we will establish an ongoing product security vulnerability reporting and response process. We welcome developers to continue reviewing ZCode and reporting potential issues, and we will provide rewards based on the severity of the issues reported.

With respect to the code data referenced by the community, we confirm that no such data is retained and that it has never been used for model training.

Following the remediation, we invited the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT) and NSFOCUS to conduct security assessments. The results are as follows:

Through its technical assessment, CAICT confirmed that the zcode-prod Alibaba Cloud OSS bucket is in a zero-data state. Security remediation has been completed in the ZCode v3.14.0 client. The Repo Wiki feature has been removed, and the workflow for generating and uploading local repository snapshots has been disabled.

NSFOCUS confirmed that all data objects in the zcode-prod Alibaba Cloud OSS bucket, as well as the bucket itself, have been deleted. Remediation has been completed in the ZCode

post.text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://github.com/

post.text:
this is f*cking insane, every app u pay for monthly is already sitting on ur disk as code, and one free repo now lets Claude Code read all of it down to the binary in 5 minutes of setup

REA is an open-source MCP server that plugs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI. it runs locally, uploads nothing and backs every answer with the function, file and call behind it

setup:

→ check Node: u need 22.19+, 24.11+ or 26+, versions 23 and 25 don't work
→ run npx rea-agents@latest setup and pick Claude Code
→ REA shows every change before making it and backs up ur config
→ restart the agent fully, closing the window isn't enough
→ run the doctor check, it only reads and tells u what to fix

engines by target:

> Electron apps like Notion, Slack, Discord: nothing extra
> .NET apps and many Unity games: nothing extra
> .exe programs and old games: Ghidra 12.1 with JDK 21
> Android APKs: JDK 17+ and JADX
> websites: any Chrome-family browser
> contract bytecode: Linux x64

limits:

> it can't touch server code, only what's on ur machine
> decompiled code is a reconstruction, so always verify
> stripped C++ binaries are much harder than Unity games

first test, send Claude Code this:

use REA to investigate how [feature] works in [app]. show the function, file and call behind every step, mark what is still unknown, write a spec with no copied code, then build my version and test it against the original

study the original, ship ur own ↓

post.text:
Someone built Git for AI agent memory.

ModernRelay has open-sourced OmniGraph, a graph database that gives AI agents something most shared-memory systems lack: branches, commits, diffs, and three-way merges.

The idea is simple. If multiple agents are working on the same knowledge base, they should be able to make changes independently without corrupting or overwriting each others work.

Imagine three agents researching the same subject. One extracts information from documents, another resolves duplicate entities, and a third connects claims to supporting evidence.

With OmniGraph, each agent works on its own branch of the knowledge graph. Changes to entities, relationships, and evidence remain isolated until they're reviewed and merged.

And this is where the engineering gets interesting.

The merge engine compares changes against a common ancestor, much like Git. It can detect conflicting entity updates, delete-versus-modify conflicts, orphaned relationships, and schema violations.

Conflicting changes are reported explicitly. Successful merges are committed atomically, and previous graph states remain available through version history.

OmniGraph also combines several retrieval methods in one engine:
→ Graph traversal for following relationships
→ Vector search for semantic similarity
→ BM25 for keyword-based retrieval
→ Reciprocal Rank Fusion for combining results

Under the hood, its written in Rust and uses versioned Lance files for storage, with support for local and

post.text:
🚨 CHROME MIGHT BE OVERKILL FOR YOUR AI AGENT.

Meet Moli.

A Rust-built headless browser designed specifically for AI agents.

The clever part?

Moli doesn't constantly render the entire visual world.

It starts with the browser structure:

→ DOM
→ JavaScript
→ CSS
→ Network
→ Storage

Need geometry? Build layout.

Need a screenshot? Render it.

Need neither? Skip the expensive visual work.

That makes browser automation much more resource-efficient.

Moli supports:
→ CDP
→ WebDriver
→ WebDriver BiDi
→ Playwright
→ Linux, macOS, Windows

And the benchmark is interesting:

Moli: 81.88% task success
Chrome: 99.85%

But Moli used roughly 15% of Chrome's CPU time and 13% of its peak memory in the project's resource comparison.

That's the tradeoff:

Less browser overhead.
Still enough web runtime for serious AI-agent workloads.

#AI #Coding #AIAgents #Rust

post.text:
看到这个帖子这么火，我不得不给大家推荐一下Orca这开源个项目了

原帖里让一个 AI 指挥一群 AI 干活的玩法过于原始了，Orca已经提供了十分棒相应的多 Agent 编排基建。

大家可以把它理解成一个 AI 编程工作台：Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 等工具放在同一个地方运行，你能统一看任务、看进度、看代码改动。

原帖提到的几个关键环节，在 Orca 里有什么更好的实现方式呢？

1. 让一个 AI 当负责人，其他 AI 分头干活

通过它的编排功能，可以让负责统筹的 Agent 拆分任务、启动其他 Agent、收集结果，再安排后续工作。

比如做一个网站，可以让 Claude 负责拆需求，Codex 写接口，另一个 Agent 检查代码。具体谁做什么，由你和负责统筹的 Agent 来定。

2. 多个任务同时跑

每个任务可以有自己的独立代码目录和分支，也就是 git worktree。一个改登录页，一个修支付接口，分别干活，最后再审查、合并结果。

还可以把同一道题交给几个 Agent 同时做，对比方案后再选。

3. 干完回报，卡住提问

它有任务状态、Agent 之间的消息和完成回报机制。执行者做完会把结果交回负责人，遇到阻塞也能提问，省掉你在几个窗口之间来回复制消息。

任务在后台推进时，你也可以继续讨论需求、补充要求，再把调整传给对应的 Agent。

4. 搭配不同模型和工具

Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode 都能接，支持列表里也有 DeepSeek Harness。想用本地模型，可以先在 OpenCode 等支持本地模型的工具里配好，再放进 Orca 使用。

模型和运行工具可以按任务搭配，不必所有活都消耗同一种模型的额度。

此外，它把查看代码差异、逐行批注、浏览器预览也放进了工作台。你可以直接指出哪一处需要改，让 Agent 接着处理。

而且手机端也很还有，远程VibeCoding爽歪歪🤩

免费开源，支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux。

https://www.onorca.dev
